units.function: Unit tests for fail-closed managed configuration parsing and a reversible read-time feature-policy overlay shared by managed-cloud and self-hosted instance settings.
units.dependencyDirection: Vitest -> managed-config parser and instance-settings service -> typed settings normalization; a minimal Db stand-in observes persistence without exercising PostgreSQL or HTTP authorization.
units.keyDataModels: Singleton instance settings row, normalized experimental feature flags, versioned managed config envelope and per-key managed metadata.
units.lifecycle: Parse deployment environment at service construction -> read tenant settings -> overlay managed values without mutation -> persist only tenant intent on update -> overlay response -> restore tenant intent when management is removed.
units.testAssessment: All 8 focused tests passed. Coverage is strong for pure precedence, self-hosted parity, non-persistence and malformed JSON, but omits real SQL/concurrency, policy authenticity, version compatibility, hot reload, route authorization and audit.
units.designRationale: Keep managed-cloud enforcement reversible and outside durable tenant configuration so one codebase supports both deployment profiles and later unmanaging does not destroy customer intent.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a single-codebase policy stack where operator constraints can govern a managed deployment without contaminating self-hosted data or silently rewriting an enterprise's chosen configuration.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the read-time effective-policy overlay, fail-closed parsing, explicit managed metadata and preservation of stored tenant intent. Generalize the hard-coded vendor identity into a signed/versioned DeploymentPolicyPort with deployment/enterprise/workspace scope, deterministic precedence, expiry, reason and immutable change receipts.
units.responsibilityConflict: The tested overlay only changes experimental features, but the same unrestricted mechanism could silently override identity, approval or responsibility semantics. Company OS must prohibit such fields or require explicit accountable-human governance and migration workflows.
units.securityFindings: HIGH policy-authenticity gap: environment JSON signature, issuer trust and tamper evidence are not tested. HIGH semantic-scope risk: no guard prevents future managed keys from changing identity/approval/responsibility behavior. MEDIUM versioning gap: v, mode and catalogVersion compatibility are not exercised. MEDIUM audit gap: effective-policy changes have no asserted receipt or notification. MEDIUM concurrency gap: real database writes and policy reload races are outside the stub. LOW branding coupling: managedBy is hard-coded to paperclip-cloud.
